newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Concern about correction grows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Concern about correction grows.

text.p: The week-long surge in U.S. stocks had some investors growing more concerned about a correction, but options traders said index call demand remained steady, with no great flocking to index puts.
"When you see the market up like it has been, I suppose you start to get worried," an options broker in Chicago said.
He said some clients have been buying puts that expire three and six months out, but that near term, investors appeared to be doing little with index options.

"You know everybody is getting nervous when they're calling you a lot," he said. "But the clients never really pull the trigger. They'll do it after we're down 200 or 300 points. But they're definitely worried."
By 1200 CST/1800 GMT, S&P 100 index .OEX call volume was 57,854 compared to 45,312 puts. S&P 500 index .SPX volume at the CBOE was split 41,864 to 31,298 in favor of calls.
"The number of phone calls I get from individual customers and brokers to hedge their portfolios with puts has been the highest ever," Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said.
He said hesitation to take action is probably a result of investors' reluctance to lay out money for an option for fear of missing another leg up in the market's rally.
"I tell them they're buying insurance," Schwartz said. "By going out-of-the-money they can put up less premium and at least be partially hedged so they don't suffer from a disaster."
Most stock indices were lower in afternoon trading Friday as investors took some profits after the week's record-setting rally, especially ahead of a three-day weekend in the U.S.
"People may be taking some positions off the table," an options trader said.
The Dow industrial average .DJI, which on Thursday posted its first close above 7,000, fell 30 points to 6,993.
The S&P 100 index .OEX slipped 1.96 at 789.26 and the S&P 500 .SPX dipped 1.95 to 809.87.

March S&P 500 futures were down 1.85 at 812.50. One firm pegged fair value at 2.40 points premium to cash, with buy programs seen at a 3.90 point premium or more and sell programs at a 1.10 point premium or less.
Among individual index options, the OEX February 790 call and put were the most active, with 15,030 and 14,300 contracts changing hands, respectively.
February 760, 765, 770, 775, 780 and 785 put also were busy, as were the 795, 800, 805 and 810 calls.
In the SPX, the September 810 call traded 10,100 contracts and the June 730 call traded 8,415, making them the most active in that pit.
